title: Pyrroloquinoline quinone disodium salt improves brain function in both younger and older adults
abstract: Brain function is important for a good quality of life. Pyrroloquinoline quinone disodium salt (PQQ) has been proven to improve brain function and cognition in older adults (above 45 years). In this double-blind, placebo-controlled study, we investigated the effects of PQQ on cognitive function in adults aged between 20 and 65 years. PQQ (20 mg per day) was administered for 12 weeks to the participants. After 12 weeks, the participants showed improvements in composite memory and verbal memory. A further age-stratified analysis was performed. In younger adults (aged 20–40 years), PQQ improved cognitive function (cognitive flexibility, processing speed, and execution speed) after 8 weeks. Only older adults (aged 41–65 years) showed improvements in complex and verbal memory after 12 weeks. In the logistic regression analysis that included the results of all cognitive tests, the changes due to PQQ intake were observed at 8 and 12 weeks in the young and old groups, respectively.
full_text: Pyrroloquinoline quinone disodium salt improves brain function in both younger and older adults. Brain function is important for a good quality of life. Pyrroloquinoline quinone disodium salt (PQQ) has been proven to improve brain function and cognition in older adults (above 45 years). In this double-blind, placebo-controlled study, we investigated the effects of PQQ on cognitive function in adults aged between 20 and 65 years. PQQ (20 mg per day) was administered for 12 weeks to the participants. After 12 weeks, the participants showed improvements in composite memory and verbal memory. A further age-stratified analysis was performed. In younger adults (aged 20–40 years), PQQ improved cognitive function (cognitive flexibility, processing speed, and execution speed) after 8 weeks. Only older adults (aged 41–65 years) showed improvements in complex and verbal memory after 12 weeks. In the logistic regression analysis that included the results of all cognitive tests, the changes due to PQQ intake were observed at 8 and 12 weeks in the young and old groups, respectively. The brain has advanced functions that are essential for life support. Cognitive function includes a variety of processes such as perception, attention, memory, decision-making, and language comprehension. Products with PQQ have been registered for use in the USA, the EU, and Japan. Pyrroloquinoline quinone disodium salt is obtained using fermentation and purification. Various functions of PQQ have been reported, including mitochondrial biogenesis, promoting longevity, antioxidant activity, and improving skin texture. In vitro studies have reported that PQQ has a strong neuroprotective effect against neurotoxicity and enhances the expression of nerve growth factor (NGF). Water maze tests in rats have shown that oral ingestion of PQQ promotes memory learning and suppresses memory loss caused by oxidative stress. The study has been registered at the UMIN Clinical Trials Registry System under UMIN ID UMIN000034459. The study was performed with a double-blind placebo control. The capsules used in the test group contained 20 mg PQQ. The capsules used in the placebo group contained starch. One capsule was taken with water after breakfast, every day. There were no adverse events associated with the test food. The test developed by CNS Vital Signs called Cognitrax was used. This test is conducted online. Of the 70 participants, 66 completed the test. The group named All included participants of all ages. The Old group included individuals aged 41–65 years. The Young group included individuals aged 20–40 years. The cognitive function showed an improvement in score with the administration of PQQ and an overall significant difference in composite memory (P = 0.003) and verbal memory (P = 0.001). In the Old group, composite memory (P = 0.011) and verbal memory (P = 0.002) improved at 12 weeks. In the age-specific analysis, some functions improved upon PQQ ingestion. There was a significant difference in cognitive flexibility, processing speed, and executive speed in the Young group at 8 weeks. Logistic regression was used for distinguishing the PQQ and placebo groups. The correct answer rate indicated differences between the groups. As the period of ingesting PQQ increased from 8 weeks to 12 weeks, the differences between the groups increased. The age-specific analysis showed improvements in the Young group in 8 weeks, with a score of 1.00. At 12 weeks, the correct answer rate of both age groups was 0.67, whereas the score of the Old group was 1.00. The effect of PQQ is closely related to the metabolism of mitochondrial neoplasia and activation. Active metabolism in young individuals could contribute to the differential improvement in cognitive function by age. Increased metabolism results in an increase in the production of reactive oxygen species. Thus, the high antioxidant activity of PQQ could contribute to improved cognitive function. Cognitive flexibility scores are associated with ADHD. PQQ increases the expression of PGC-1a, whose levels are elevated during sports activities. In summary, PQQ improves cognitive functions of cognitive flexibility and executive speed within 8 weeks in young adults aged 20–40 years. Cognitive functions of composite and verbal memories are improved after 12 weeks in adults aged 20–65 years. PQQ is a functional food that improves brain function at any age.

conditions.name: Cognitive Decline
conditions.efficacy_description: Significant improvements in composite memory (p=0.003) and verbal memory (p=0.001) after 12 weeks in the overall population. Younger adults showed earlier improvements (8 weeks) in processing speed and cognitive flexibility.

mechanisms.name: ↑ PGC-1α expression
mechanisms.description: PQQ stimulates mitochondrial biogenesis through increased PGC-1α expression. This mechanism enhances cellular metabolism and energy production, which is particularly beneficial for high-energy demanding tissues like the brain.

mechanisms.name: ↑ Nerve growth factor (NGF) expression
mechanisms.description: PQQ enhances the expression of nerve growth factor (NGF), an essential protein for the growth, maintenance, and survival of certain target neurons, conferring strong neuroprotective effects.

interactions.description: PQQ administration increases the expression of PGC-1α, driving mitochondrial biogenesis.
PQQ enhances the expression of nerve growth factor (NGF) in neural tissues.
Upregulation of PGC-1α directly stimulates mitochondrial activation and biogenesis.
PQQ acts directly as a strong antioxidant, reducing reactive oxygen species.
Reduction in oxidative stress suppresses memory loss and improves cognitive function.
Increased NGF expression provides neuroprotective effects against neurotoxicity and cognitive deterioration.
Neuroprotection and enhanced mitochondrial function collectively mitigate cognitive decline.

side_effects.name: No adverse events reported
side_effects.description: No adverse events or serious adverse events associated with the test food were observed during the 12-week study. Blood tests, urine tests, and physical examinations remained normal.

studySummary.objective: To investigate the effects of pyrroloquinoline quinone disodium salt (PQQ) on cognitive function in healthy adults aged between 20 and 65 years across a 12-week double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
limitations: Did not specifically evaluate subjects with existing cognitive impairments or ADHD (only healthy volunteers).
Relatively short study duration of 12 weeks.
Did not directly measure blood biomarkers for mitochondrial biogenesis or oxidative stress to correlate with cognitive outcomes.
key_findings: PQQ (20 mg/day) significantly improved composite memory (P=0.003) and verbal memory (P=0.001) in adults aged 20-65 years over 12 weeks.
In younger adults (20-40 years), PQQ improved cognitive flexibility, processing speed, and executive speed after just 8 weeks.
Logistic regression utilizing machine learning on cognitive test results could accurately distinguish between PQQ and placebo groups, showing efficacy increases with ingestion time.
Different age groups exhibited distinct cognitive benefits from PQQ, with young adults responding faster in processing/executive functions and older adults improving in memory.
studySummary.clinical_implications: PQQ can be effectively utilized as a functional nutraceutical to enhance brain function across all age groups, not just the elderly. It may support cognitive flexibility and processing speed in younger populations while preserving memory in older populations. Translates well to veterinary medicine for managing age-related cognitive decline in companion animals.

contraindications.reason: Pregnant women, nursing women, and those wishing to become pregnant were excluded from the study as a standard safety precaution for non-essential dietary supplements.
